production.headline: Public launch needs Extended Quota Mode, which Spotify now offers only to registered organizations with a launched service and 250k+ monthly active users.

verdict.confidence: high on the gates, medium on how strictly they are enforced today
verdict.summary: Spotify is easy to try and hard to ship. Anyone can build a working integration for 5 people. There is no documented route for a small team to go from 5 users to a public launch. If you do not already meet the Extended Quota criteria, plan for Spotify to stay a limited or internal integration.

stages.name: Decide what you are building for

steps.text: Count the people who will need to connect Spotify. If it is 5 or fewer, Development Mode is enough. If it is more, jump to stage 7 and check eligibility before you build.

stages.name: Get a Spotify Premium account and create the app

steps.text: Sign in to the Spotify Developer Dashboard with a Premium account. The app owner needs Premium for a Development Mode app to function.
Click Create an App, enter an app name and description (users see both on the consent screen), accept the Developer Terms, and create it.
Plan for one Development Mode Client ID per developer. Do not create separate apps for dev and staging. Add several redirect URIs to the one app instead.

stages.name: Get the redirect URI from Composio and register it with Spotify

steps.text: In the Composio dashboard go to Auth Configs, click Create Auth Config, select Spotify and choose OAuth2. The dashboard shows the redirect URI to use.

In your Spotify app, open Edit Settings and paste that URI into Redirect URIs. Spotify requires HTTPS (loopback IPs are the only HTTP exception, and localhost is not allowed), so check that the Composio URI is accepted when you save.

Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the Spotify app overview into the Composio auth config, click Create, and copy the auth config ID (it looks like ac_xxxx). Keep the secret out of source control.
Pass the ID to your session: authConfigs: { spotify: "ac_..." }. Toolkits you do not list keep using Composio managed auth.
In the Dashboard open your app, then Settings, then User Management, and add each tester's name and Spotify email. A person who is not on the list can still log in, but their API calls return 403.
The agent generates a Connect Link with session.authorize("spotify"), then checks the connected account status until it is ACTIVE. The developer or tester completes the Spotify consent screen.
The agent runs a read call as an allowlisted user to confirm it works, then as a non-allowlisted user to confirm the 403.

stages.name: Apply for Extended Quota Mode (only if you need more than 5 users)
stages.effort: Unknown. Needs a legal entity, a company email and a questionnaire.

steps.text: Check the six requirements first: legal business entity, active launched service, at least 250k monthly active users, availability in key Spotify markets, commercial viability, adherence to terms. If you do not meet them, stop here.
Submit the Partner Application form from a company email. Applications from individuals are not accepted.

If approved, open the app in the Dashboard, go to Settings, then the Quota extension Request tab, complete the 4-step questionnaire and submit. The status shows Sent. Feedback arrives by email, so make sure that inbox is monitored.

requirements: Spotify Premium account on the app owner (Development Mode)
HTTPS redirect URI exactly matching what is registered (loopback IP literals are the only HTTP exception; localhost is not allowed)
For public launch: legally registered organization, launched service, 250k+ monthly active users, availability in key Spotify markets, commercial viability, policy compliance
A monitored email address on the Spotify developer account (review feedback goes there)

blockers.issue: The 6th user cannot use the app
blockers.whenItHits: As soon as you invite more than 5 users in Development Mode
blockers.whatToDo: Remove inactive testers from the allowlist, or move to Extended Quota Mode if you qualify. Otherwise keep the integration internal.

blockers.issue: No documented path between 5 users and the 250k MAU bar
blockers.whenItHits: When you try to grow past a closed beta
blockers.whatToDo: Decide early whether Spotify is a launch feature or a nice-to-have. Developers in the community report asking and getting no separate small-project route. Treat this as a product risk, not a setup step.

blockers.issue: Dev-mode request quota is shared across your apps
blockers.whatToDo: Expect 429 responses with reason QUOTA_EXCEEDED. This is a different limit from the 30-second rate limit. Back off and reduce polling.

blockers.whenItHits: When you plan how many apps you can create
blockers.whatToDo: The Apps page says up to 25 apps per account. Spotify's February 2026 announcement says new Development Mode accounts get one Client ID. Trust the dated announcement and confirm in your Dashboard.

blockers.issue: Some endpoints or fields may be unavailable to new apps
blockers.whenItHits: When a call that worked in older tutorials returns an error or missing fields
blockers.whatToDo: Check Spotify's February 2026 changelog for the endpoints your use case needs before you build around them.

claims.text: New Spotify apps start in Development Mode.
The app owner must have Spotify Premium for a Development Mode app to function.

Up to 5 authenticated users can use a Development Mode app. Each must be on the allowlist (Dashboard > app > Settings > User Management). Non-allowlisted users may log in, but API requests with their token return 403.
App creation: click Create an App, enter name and description (shown on the grant screen), accept Developer Terms. Redirect URIs are set in Edit Settings and one or more can be listed.

Extended Quota applications are accepted only from organizations (since 15 May 2025), through a form sent from a company email. Requirements: established business entity, active launched service, at least 250k MAUs, availability in key Spotify markets, commercial viability, adherence to terms.

After the Partner Application is approved, you request the move in the Dashboard (Quota extension Request tab, 4-step questionnaire). The status shows Sent, feedback comes by email, and review can take up to six weeks.

Redirect URIs must use HTTPS, except loopback IP literals (http://127.0.0.1:PORT or http://[::1]:PORT). localhost is not allowed. The URI must match the registered one exactly, except for the port on loopback addresses.

Spotify documents three flows: authorization code, authorization code with PKCE, and client credentials. The implicit grant is not in the current list, although the Redirect URIs page still mentions it.
Client credentials cannot access user resources, so it cannot back a per-user connection like the ones Composio manages.

Development Mode has a request quota counted across the apps of one developer account, grouped into endpoint buckets. Exceeding it returns 429 with reason QUOTA_EXCEEDED. This is separate from the rate limit.
Spotify's 6 Feb 2026 announcement: Development Mode Client IDs created from 11 Feb 2026 require Premium, are limited to one Client ID per developer, and allow up to five authorized users.
The Apps documentation page still says up to 25 apps per developer account. This conflicts with c11 and is probably stale, because the announcement is newer and dated.

On 9 March Spotify postponed endpoint-access changes for existing Development Mode integrations. A staff reply in the community thread says the Premium requirement, user cap and one-Client-ID limit still apply to existing integrations.

Developers on the community forum report no separate small-project route to Extended Quota, and one who registered a company and applied reported being unsure about next steps. These are individual reports, not Spotify policy.
Some endpoints and response fields changed for new Development Mode apps in February 2026. The exact list was not read for this guide.
Spotify is on Composio's list of OAuth toolkits where the developer must bring their own OAuth app (no Composio-managed app).
